_note: Four-layer rumour pool. Accuracy is not guaranteed; the pool contains false information on purpose. Some entries point at clues but write no flag. See NARRATIVE_DRAFTS 4.9.2. In the maplegate layer, entries 1, 3 and 4 are false; entry 4 contradicts Gregor’s GRE-P1 fragment outright, which is the point.
intro:
The square is fuller in the afternoon than it was this morning.

You bring the cart round to the east side and take third place in the line behind the grain merchant’s stall. The man in front is haggling and looks set to be a while.

Standing in a queue at a market is a particular condition. You are doing nothing at all, and you can hear everything.
local: The miller’s daughter is marrying south. Two cows in the dowry, which counts as handsome around here.
Somebody fished a shoe out of the river bend. One shoe. They talked it over for an hour and got nowhere.
The boundary stake on the eastern holding was moved last year. Not two feet. The two families still do not speak when they meet.
Old Wendt’s grandson wants to go to Valehold and take an apprenticeship. His grandfather will not have it. Says work in a field is no worse than work in a shop.
The frost is earlier than usual this year. Some say that is a good thing, that a year with an early frost has a short winter.
duchy: The felling allowance for the north district is tighter this year than it has been. Some say the duchy wants the woods kept. Others say somebody filed the wrong numbers and it is being looked into.
The Duke’s hunting party spent six days out west last month. Thirty-odd people, and one stag to show for it. Some say she was not there to hunt at all.
The rate may be adjusted next year. The man who says so says it at this time every year.
That forester’s post was never going to come to him. Third son of a count. By rights he should have gone into the army or into a marriage.
That inspector from the chancery. Nobody has got him to a dinner from one year’s end to the next. Some say he is above it. Some say he cannot afford to return the invitation.
kingdom: The Crown Prince and his wife, both their Highnesses, are a matched pair made for each other. The man saying so has never laid eyes on either of them.
After the Collegium his Highness stayed abroad for his degrees. He has the doctorate now and there is still no sign of him coming home.
“It is not that his Highness does not want to come home. It is that he cannot well come home. You have seen His Majesty these last few years —” and there he stops.
People up from Forgehold say there was bad feeling between his Highness and the family, and that is why he went so far. Nobody can say what it was over. There is always somebody who knows a little.
The Eisenbach house has gone downhill these few years. Something happened to the eldest son. Too many versions of what to be worth repeating; the upshot is that he cannot run anything.
It is the second son holding it up now. Barely twenty-something, and what he took on is a heap of bad accounts.
The money old Duke Ferdinand owed: some say it got mixed in with the duchy’s own books. Even the man saying it will not swear to it.
That lot in Flamincore want to put on some kind of carriage race. Truly. Carriages, on a road, to see who is fastest. There is a great row about it in Forgehold.
The theology those scholars in Luminveil make. A new account of it every year, and last year’s does not line up with this year’s.
Their people are very civil when they speak to you. Civilly, they tell you that you stand outside the Sacred Flame, and so you have no say in the matter.
One of the contemplatives said that those scholars stand in front of the Flame and never feel It, being too busy taking It apart and studying It. That sounded right to me.
The old duke at Luminhold is not well. His two children are fighting over it.
The ducal house of Ridgecrest is genuinely devoted to the Crown. Three generations of it, and each one plainer than the last.
What nobody knows is who comes after. There is no child in that generation of theirs that anyone has heard of.
I heard from my cousin’s husband’s cousin, who worked a while in a Forgehold smithy, that his Grace has never been with any woman at all. You understand me.
You get every sort of person over in Stormgale. On the docks you will meet people from places you have never heard the name of.
Forgehold people say half of what Stormgale calls trade should be called smuggling. Stormgale people say Forgehold has never seen the sea.
The Havner house is doing business with foreigners again. Forgehold is said to be less than pleased.
maplegate: They say that steward at Maplegate ran off owing money.
There is a foreigner at Maplegate now. People have seen him. Speaks with an accent, but reckons up fast.
Baron von Alder has not shown his face in Valehold in ten years.
That steward sold one of the estate’s horses before he went.
